7ai.status_detail: Operating; latest round is the $130M Series A announced 2025-12-04, no later round found.
7ai.note: Index led the Series A and Shardul Shah joined the board; the release lists Greylock, CRV and Spark as the existing seed investors, not Index. WSJ reported a $700M valuation for the Series A (seen via SecurityWeek summary), so below $1B. Form D for the round filed 2025-12-04.

artbinder.status_detail: Acquired by Volaris Group (Constellation Software) in November 2022, price undisclosed; artbinder.com now redirects to Gallery Systems.
artbinder.note: TechCrunch names the $3.17M round a Series A led by Index, announced 2014-07-01; the matching Form D was filed 2014-05-13, so I dated the entry 2014-05. Acquisition source: https://www.volarisgroup.com/press-room/artbinder-acquired-by-volaris-group/ (seen in search results) and the live redirect to gallerysystems.com.

cartesia.status_detail: Operating; latest round is the $100M round of October 2025 led by Kleiner Perkins, no reported valuation.
cartesia.note: Company's own post: $27M seed led by Index (the $22M Index-led tranche brought the total to $27M). Series A $64M led by Kleiner Perkins, March 2025 (https://cartesia.ai/blog/series-a). No priced round with a reported valuation found; the $200M/$400M figures online are data-vendor estimates, not counted. No 2026 round found.

catch.status_detail: Appears to have ceased operating around 2025: getcatch.com (the site Index lists) is now a parked domain, merchant Catch pages are gone, and a search snippet states it is no longer operational as of 2025-04-24; no shutdown announcement found.
catch.note: IDENTITY CONFLICT WITH THE BRIEF: the firm's own page (indexventures.com/companies/catch/) describes the pay-by-bank rewards company at getcatch.com (founders Nico Perdomo, Denia Ebersole, Vijay Singh, Whitney LaRow; partner Danny Rimer), not the freelancer-benefits Catch (catch.co, Kristen Anderson), which I found no Index link to. I classified the getcatch.com company. Status is weakly sourced: I could not open the page behind the 'no longer operational' snippet, last press coverage is May 2024, CB Insights still shows it alive; treat as defunct-leaning-unknown. No source says which round Index joined (Sequoia's page says it partnered in 2020; vendor round lists disagree). HQ: Payments Dive (May 2023) says San Francisco, Built In lists New York. If the row is meant to be catch.co instead: that company announced its shutdown (Finextra/FinTech Futures headlines), also defunct.

clickhouse.status_detail: Operating; closed a $400M Series D led by Dragoneer on 2026-01-16 at a reported $15B valuation.
clickhouse.note: $50M Series A led by Index and Benchmark when ClickHouse, Inc. was spun out of Yandex (announced September 2021; Index's own post dates the incorporation to August 2021). HQ: Index says 'Bay Area', the company's releases are datelined San Francisco. No round after January 2026 found.

crossing-minds.status_detail: Team joined OpenAI in June 2025 (acqui-hire) and the company's site said it would take no more clients; no sign of operation since.
crossing-minds.note: Index was in the $3.5M raised before the September 2018 launch (with Sound Ventures and You & Mr Jones); TechCrunch does not name that round, I read it as the seed because the October 2021 $10M Series A (led by Radical) lists Index as an existing investor (https://techcrunch.com/2021/10/18/crossing-minds-brings-in-new-capital-to-provide-recommendations-that-dont-require-identifiable-information/). Status: no formal dissolution found; crossingminds.com returns 403 to me. Source for the end: https://techcrunch.com/2025/06/27/openai-hires-team-behind-ai-recommendation-startup-crossing-minds/.

decagon.status_detail: Operating; $250M Series D in January 2026 at $4.5B, and a tender offer at the same valuation in March 2026.
decagon.note: Index co-led the Series D with Coatue; Bloomberg lists a16z, Accel and Bain Capital Ventures as the existing investors, so this is Index's first round. No later priced round found.

dorsia.status_detail: Operating (site live, Dorsia events in 2026); latest round is the $50.4M announced 2025-02-13, reported by Bloomberg at a $146M valuation.
dorsia.note: The company announced the $50.4M as 'seed and Series A funding' in one go, with the round led by Index. I could not establish whether Index was already in the seed part; I read the Index-led financing as the Series A (aggregators label it Series A, and Index's company page has no earlier capture). If Index was in the seed, entry_stage would be Seed and graduated. HQ Miami per Refresh Miami; one aggregator says New York.

duna.status_detail: Operating; raised a EUR 30M Series A led by CapitalG in February 2026.
duna.note: Index led the EUR 10.7M seed in May 2025 and joined the Series A (also stated in Index's own post). No valuation reported. HQ is the soft spot: TechCrunch says 'based in Germany and the Netherlands'; Dutch press calls it a Dutch company, I chose Amsterdam without a registry check.

enigma.status_detail: Operating; emerged from stealth on 2026-07-27 with a $71M seed led by Index and Ribbit.
enigma.note: Entry date: Index's post says the deal was agreed 'on a warm spring night last year' (2025), before incorporation; the $71M seed was announced 2026-07. Either way the seed is under 24 months old with no later round. No valuation reported. HQ uncertain: legal entity is Enigma AI Labs Inc. (US), but the site's terms are governed by Israeli law with Tel Aviv courts, CTech calls it an Israeli startup and the team is Israeli; Dealroom lists San Francisco. Focus could equally be AI & Applied AI (the firm tags it AI/ML).

feathery.status_detail: Operating; announced a Series A led by Portage in July 2026 (total funding $30M).
feathery.note: Seed of $4.5M in 2021 co-led by Index and Bain Capital Ventures, per secondary write-ups of the 2026 release (FinTech Futures page was blocked; Business Wire headline dated 2026-07-14). Month of the seed not found. Sources disagree on whether $30M is the Series A or the total raised. No valuation reported. Now sells to financial services firms, so Fintech & Payments is a defensible alternative focus.

figma.status_detail: Listed on the NYSE (FIG) since its IPO on 2025-07-31.
figma.note: Index led the roughly $4M seed (Form D 2013 Q2, $4.0M); Series A $14M led by Greylock in December 2015. Market cap is close to the $10B line: $11.69B on 2026-10-06, down from $18.5B at end of 2025.

frontback.status_detail: Announced a shutdown in July 2015, then an unnamed partner took over the product in August 2015 on confidential terms; the founders left.
frontback.note: Index entered in the $910K seed of Checkthis (the company behind Frontback), led by Lerer. The later round of about $3M (October 2013) was unnamed and under $5M, so not graduated. Status is a judgement call: the business was handed to a new owner rather than closed (https://techcrunch.com/2015/08/03/frontback-is-back-with-a-new-team/), so I read it as acquired; the buyer was never named in what I found and the app later disappeared, so defunct is the alternative reading. Moved from New York to San Francisco in 2013.

innovative-silicon.status_detail: Closed on 2010-06-29; its patent portfolio was bought by Micron in December 2010.
innovative-silicon.note: Index led the $6M 'first round of venture capital funding' (announced 2004-03-17; the company's 2005 release says it closed in 2003). No source I read literally calls it Series A; I label it so because the next round was announced as Series B (June 2005, led by Austin Ventures, https://design-reuse.com/news/10755/innovative-silicon-secures-16m-b-funding.html). Status: I chose defunct because the company closed and only the patents were sold afterwards; if a post-closure IP sale counts as a sale of assets, the row would be acquired (Micron, 2010, undisclosed). Incorporated in the US (Santa Clara) with R&D in Lausanne. Semiconductor IP has no exact focus bucket.

king.status_detail: Acquired by Activision Blizzard for $5.9B, closed 2016-02-23 (it had been NYSE-listed since March 2014).
king.note: Index and Apax bought into King.com in 2005 in a $43M round that was largely secondary; no source I found names it seed, Series A or anything else, so entry_stage is undetermined (in substance it was a growth-style deal in a profitable company, and its only outside round before the IPO). Wikipedia lists the headquarters as Stockholm and London; I took Stockholm.

mirelo.status_detail: Operating; latest round is the $41M seed announced 2025-12-15.
mirelo.note: Seed co-led by Index and Andreessen Horowitz; the earlier pre-seed was led by Atlantic, not Index (TechCrunch 2025-12-15). Valuation not disclosed. No later round found, seed is under 24 months old.

move-loot.status_detail: Ceased operations in June 2016; only access to its customer list was sold to Handy, no other assets or staff.
move-loot.note: $2.8M seed led by First Round and Index. Graduation rests on the $9M round of February 2015 led by Metamorphic (not named Series A by TechCrunch, but more than twice the seed and over $5M). End: https://techcrunch.com/2016/06/29/move-loot-a-yc-backed-furniture-resale-marketplace-shuts-down-sells-customer-list-to-handy/.

nacelle.status_detail: Still operating as a small team: nacelle.com is live in October 2026 and sells 'Nacelle Delta', a post-click optimisation product for Shopify stores.
nacelle.note: $4.8M seed led by Index and Accomplice (called a seed in the Series A coverage: https://techcrunch.com/2021/01/12/e-commerce-infrastructure-startup-nacelle-closes-18m-series-a/); Series A $18M led by Inovia (January 2021), Series B $50M from Tiger Global (August 2021). No valuation was reported for any round. The company has clearly shrunk and changed product; I found no acquisition or shutdown news.

numberfour.status_detail: NumberFour AG (trading as enfore) filed for insolvency on 2024-09-26; founder Marco Boerries reportedly bought the remains in 2025 and the product continues at newpos.ai.
numberfour.note: $38M Series A led by Index (Mike Volpi), announced 2013-06-26; a convertible round preceded it and I could not tell whether Index was in that. The purchase out of insolvency rests on a search-result summary of a September 2025 report plus Manager Magazin headlines of 2025-09-19; I could not open the article. enfore.com now redirects to newpos.ai. Insolvency court was Berlin-Charlottenburg; the company also ran from Hamburg. Insolvency source: https://www.echo24.de/welt/vom-zweiten-sap-in-die-insolvenz-software-start-up-steht-vor-unsicherer-zukunft-zr-93327046.html.

pentaho.status_detail: Acquired by Hitachi Data Systems, completed June 2015, for a reported $500-600M.
pentaho.note: $5M Series A led by NEA with Index (Computerwoche, 2005-12-09; also https://techcrunch.com/2012/10/30/open-source-business-intelligence-company-pentaho-lands-23-million-series-c/). The price was never officially disclosed; press put it at $500-600M. Wikipedia says Pentaho was sold on again to LEO Software in June 2026, which I did not verify.

physical-intelligence.status_detail: Operating; latest confirmed priced round is the $600M round of November 2025 led by CapitalG at $5.6B.
physical-intelligence.note: Index is named as a new investor in the November 2025 round, which is widely labelled Series B (seed March 2024, Series A November 2024, neither with Index). VALUATION IS NEAR A BAND EDGE: a roughly $1B round at $11B was reported as talks in March 2026, and aggregators cite a charter filing of 2026-05-21 authorising about $1.05B of Series C stock at $11-11.2B; the company has not confirmed it and TechCrunch on 2026-07-21 still wrote 'reportedly in talks'. I did not count it; if it is accepted as closed the range becomes 10b_plus. Focus could equally be AI & Applied AI (the firm tags it AI/ML).

spendesk.status_detail: Operating (new products and reports through 2026); last priced round is the EUR 100M Series C extension from Tiger Global in January 2022.
spendesk.note: Index's own post: 'a EUR 8M Series A led by Index Ventures' in January 2018; Index then led the Series B in 2019. Valuation: the company said 'more than $1.14 billion' (more than EUR 1B) in January 2022; a Bloomberg headline put it at $1.5B. Both are in the same band; no later priced round found.

tessl-io.status_detail: Operating (tessl.io live, now an 'agent enablement platform'); latest round is the $100M Series A announced November 2024.
tessl-io.note: Index led the Series A; the $25M seed was co-led by GV and boldstart without Index. Form D for the $100M filed 2024-11-15. Valuation reported at $500M+ (TechCrunch) to $750M (Fortune/City AM), so below $1B. No later round found. Focus could also be AI & Applied AI.

topi.status_detail: Acquired by PEAC Solutions, announced 2025-08-27, price undisclosed; topi continues to operate from Berlin.
topi.note: $4.5M pre-seed co-led by Index and Creandum. Graduation rests on the August 2022 round of $15M equity (plus $30M debt), which TechCrunch does not name; it is more than twice the pre-seed and over $5M. If that round was formally a 'seed', a stricter reading would say not_graduated. Acquisition source: https://www.dentons.com/en/about-dentons/news-events-and-awards/news/2025/august/dentons-advises-peac-solutions-on-acquisition-of-fintech-company-topi.

trello.status_detail: Acquired by Atlassian for $425M, announced January 2017 and closed in early 2017.
trello.note: $10.3M Series A co-led by Index and Spark when Trello was spun out of Fog Creek. Price source: https://techcrunch.com/2017/01/09/atlassian-acquires-trello/. The exact closing month (February 2017) is from memory, not re-checked.

tweetup.status_detail: Renamed PostUp, then UberMedia; acquired by Near in April 2021, terms undisclosed.
tweetup.note: Index led the $3.5M 'first round of funding' at launch (Danny Rimer on the board; Form D filed July 2010). Every source I read says 'first round', none says seed or Series A, and I could not confirm how the next round ($17.5M, 2011) was named, so entry_stage is undetermined; databases tend to call it Series A. Acquisition source: https://techcrunch.com/2021/04/28/near-acquires-ubermedia/.

typeform.status_detail: Operating independently as far as I can establish; last priced round is the $135M Series C of March 2022 at a $935M post-money valuation.
typeform.note: Index's own post: 'a $15m Series A in 2015, led by Index' (October 2015 from memory). Valuation source: https://techcrunch.com/2022/03/10/typeform-series-c/. CONTESTED STATUS: Bloomberg reported in October 2025 that Bending Spoons was looking to buy Typeform, and two aggregator pages claim a completed $255M acquisition. I found no confirmation: Bending Spoons' August 2026 6-K and its website list its businesses without Typeform, and typeform.com does not mention Bending Spoons. If the sale did close, the row is acquired, still below_1b.

vouch.status_detail: Operating as Vouch Group, Inc. in San Francisco (new COO hired July 2026); sold its MGA and carrier operations to Hiscox in 2025 and continues as a broker.
vouch.note: $24.5M Series A led by Ribbit and SVB with YC, Index and 500 Startups, announced September 2019 (TechCrunch says it closed earlier that year). Last reported valuation is $550M at the 2021 Series C; a $25M Series C-1 led by Ribbit in March 2024 came without a reported valuation. The Hiscox deal covered only part of the business, so I kept the status private.
